Thanks for a great call earlier, Sofia — appreciate the clear context on use case and procurement timelines. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap:
- Primary use case: real-time risk-scoring and large embedding index for customer transactions (low-latency inference at scale).
- Traffic expectation: ~100M tokens/month initially, ramp to ~300M in 6–9 months.
- Security constraints: data residency in US, SOC2 required, customer-managed KMS is preferred but not required on day one.

Procurement path options we discussed (need your preference):
1) Marketplace (AWS Marketplace) + PO: Preferred by many FinTech procurement teams because it can streamline invoicing and allow PO issuance against the marketplace listing.
2) Direct vendor invoice (card or net-30 PO): we can invoice directly; net-30 requires vendor onboarding paperwork (W-9, vendor form).
3) Dedicated/Private procurement: if you require a Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment we’ll treat this as an enterprise contract with longer lead time and an annual reserved commit.

Packaging & pricing summary (attached):
- Hosted (on-demand): fastest to start, pay-as-you-go, no commit required. Good for proofs-of-concept and initial ramp.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput and lower unit cost with 12/24-month commits; SLA-backed latency.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for strict data control—multi-week deployment and additional platform license fee.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Sofia: can procurement confirm if they prefer marketplace PO vs direct PO (card/net-30)? This will determine which quote template we send.
- Sofia / procurement: share vendor onboarding form if you have one; I’ll loop in our procurement lead to complete it.
- Aditya (cc): will follow up with a short note on performance and sizing guidance for dedicated vs hosted.
- I’ll attach a formal one-page quote based on your preference and include SOC2 and DPAs.

Attachments: FinTechCo_Redwood_Pricing_Options_Q3_2026.pdf (pricing + packaging), SOC2_Report_Redwood_2025.pdf (security background)

Thanks — I’ll wait to hear procurement’s preference and will prepare the appropriate quote.

Hey Sofia — quick technical note on packaging/price tradeoffs so procurement has context: 

1) Hosted (on-demand):
- Pros: immediate start, no provisioning lead time, billed per-token.
- Cons: higher per-token unit cost vs committed capacity; unpredictable at high variance.
- Estimate for your 100M tokens/month: ~$0.018/token effective unit (example line item — see attached quote for exact math).

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Pros: consistent latency (SLO), lower unit cost if you commit (12- or 24-month term), supports heavy concurrent workloads.
- Cons: commit required, provisioning lead time ~2–4 weeks to allocate GPU pool.
- Example delta: for steady 300M tokens/month, commit pricing can reduce effective unit cost by ~30–45% vs hosted on-demand.

3) Private / VPC:
- Pros: strongest controls (network isolation, customer KMS).
- Cons: license + infra integration; longer procurement/ops timeline; often negotiated as an enterprise contract.

For procurement TCO, the typical approach we recommend: start hosted to validate latency and quality, move to a dedicated committed pool once you hit predictable throughput (we can build an early-commit pilot with a 3–6 month “pilot commit” discount to bridge that gap).

Happy to run a quick cost model if you share expected token volumes by month (1–6 months).

— Aditya
